summary: Configured node1 as a persistent, read-only TFTP server for the approved boot subtree. Node2 downloads both files with exact hashes; uploads and outside-root access are rejected. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL 10-supported tftp-server package without changing the OS release or kernel.
Published only /srv/legacy2/tftp-firmware-distribution/boot as the secure TFTP root.
Applied read-only permissions, persistent SELinux labels, systemd confinement, socket activation, and firewall rules.
Verified boot.cfg and firmware.bin transfers from node2 and exact SHA-256 preservation.
Verified new uploads, overwrites, and path traversal requests are rejected.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified post-restart recovery.

evidence.requirement: Publish the approved boot tree as a persistent read-only TFTP root
evidence.summary: The secure TFTP root points directly at the boot subtree; permissions are read-only, SELinux labels are correct, and socket/firewall configuration is persistent.

evidence.requirement: Node2 can download boot.cfg and firmware.bin with firmware bytes preserved
evidence.summary: Source and node2 download SHA-256 hashes match exactly for both files before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Reject uploads and requests outside the boot root
evidence.summary: New-file upload, overwrite, and traversal requests failed; no unauthorized file exists in the TFTP root.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c to 826e3154-5143-4eea-82d9-dc0417fc3a80; TFTP, firewall, files, and live transfers recovered.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node2 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 to a09a8cbb-ceba-4b50-9bcc-bf1b17a7c5cd; firewall state, downloads, hashes, and rejection behavior recovered.
